correctness.rationale: Strict TP2 of Bernstein kernels persists under positive composition, and reflection produces a unique midpoint sign crossing of endpoint-row densities. BV signed-jump decomposition reduces the sharp variation norm and equality classification to the midpoint step. Shifted Legendre eigenvalues yield the finite odd-degree sum and all-power asymptotic; decreasing alternating terms certify sharp two-mode bounds; uniqueness proves strict submultiplicativity. Independent exact rational Gram-matrix checks agree for 96 integer pairs (\(n\le12\), \(r\le8\)) and independently test critical identities. No finite calculation is used as a proof for all n,r.

originality.rationale: The archival 2016 paper proves nonsharp variation diminution; the complete accessible indexed Jacobi-weighted sharp oscillation finding gives the unweighted one-step factor and explicitly leaves arbitrary iterates open. The 2025 all-power kernel eigenexpansion and the Heilmann–Raşa 2016 iterate theory supply prerequisites, not the sharp all-power real-BV variation norm, midpoint equality classification, or strict power submultiplicativity. Combining known eigenvalues with the newly supplied strict-TP2/unique-crossing argument yields an exact all-power formula. Historical completeness is not certified.

value.rationale: The exact power norm describes the optimal stability of repeated smoothing on real BV. The known one-step factor \(1-2^{-n}\) is exponentially close to one in n, while the sharp long-power decay uses spectral rate \(n/(n+2)\) and universal prefactor \(3/2\). The midpoint equality classification, two-mode quantitative bounds, and strict submultiplicativity resolve a natural stability gap; not a mere parameter relabeling or arbitrarily selected finite case.
